claim: Session 28 phase 2 compilation of cell_sim/layer3_reactions/gene_expression.py rules into the FastEventSimulator's vectorised compiled-spec path drops the gex-on per-run wall-time slowdown from the phase-1 measurement of 3.60x (memory_bank/facts/measured/phase1_gex_wiring_wall_measurement.json) to 1.29x, on the same 5-knockout sample (1 WT + 4 single-gene KOs) at scale_factor=0.05, t_end_s=0.5, sample_dt_s=0.05, seed=42, use_rust_backend=False. Mean per-run wall: 17.29 s (gex_off) vs 22.35 s (gex_on). Total: 86.45 s vs 111.75 s. Hits the FUTURE_WORK.md success criterion (<1.30x). The gex-off path remains byte-identical to the phase-1 layout, verified by cell_sim/tests/test_phase2_gex_off_bit_identity.py at every commit in the phase-2 chain.
source_detail: Reproducible by running 'python scripts/_measure_phase2_wall.py' from the repo root. Output JSON at outputs/phase2_wall_measurement.json. Code path measured: cell_sim.layer6_essentiality.real_simulator.RealSimulator.run with enable_gene_expression=True vs False on the same 5-knockout sample. Phase-2 commits on claude/syn3a-whole-cell-simulator-REjHC: 9273d57 (step 2: vectorised gex partition), d1de4fe (step 3: factories emit compiled_spec), 2dad436 (step 4: rust backend mirror via shared helpers), and a chain of micro-optimisations described in the value.optimisation_chain block below.

optimisation_chain.note: Move gex from python-closure to dedicated vectorised partition; py cache no longer thrashed on gex events but the per-step categorical sampling loop still scales as O(n_rules).
Replace the O(n_rules) Python sampling loop with np.cumsum + np.searchsorted; bit-identical for gex-off.
Replace per-iteration python-rule props scatter with self._props += self._py_props_cache; drop the per-step cands_scratch rebuild and read cands directly from _py_cands_cache at apply time.
Stop setting _gex_counts_dirty on python-closure fires (folding/complex/protein_degrade/etc never mutate state.mrna_counts or machinery scalars).
Drop redundant where-masks in the gex propensity formula (n_mrna * machinery already gives 0 when either is 0; only tx needs the rnap>0 mask).
Cache the gex propensity vector and recompute only on (a) gex/python fires, (b) per-rule gating-substrate threshold flips.

Add a 2-scalar-comparison fast path: if every gating substrate's count is at least its per-substrate max threshold AND the previous compute observed all gates open AND the dirty flag is clear, skip the per-rule gate_disabled allocation entirely.

caveats: Sample size of 5 knockouts is the same as the phase-1 measurement, kept identical for direct comparison. Per-knockout variance is ~1 s/run; the gex_off vs gex_on gap (~5 s/run) is large enough that the 1.29x ratio is robust against noise but not deeply tight.

Use_rust_backend=False matches the phase-1 measurement. With Rust on, the absolute walls drop ~2x but the gex_off baseline drops more than gex_on (the gex propensity calc stays in Python under both backends), so the slowdown ratio under Rust is expected to be higher than 1.29x. A separate Rust+gex-on measurement should be made before claiming the criterion holds for the full Rust-backed sweep.

The 1.29x ratio is at the FUTURE_WORK.md success criterion (<1.30x) but only barely. Optimisations beyond this point (compiling protein-degradation, fine-grained python-closure cache invalidation) were considered and deferred — protein-degradation in particular still consumes ~7% of gex-on cumulative time via repeated can_fire calls on python-cache invalidation by folding events. The prompt explicitly held protein-degradation as python-closure ('low rate, touches protein-instance buckets, not worth the refactor').

Gex-on bit-identity vs the slow EventSimulator reference is NOT verified by an existing test fixture. The cell_sim/tests/test_fast_equivalence.py suite exercises Priority-1.5 (folding + complex assembly + reversible catalysis) without gene expression. The wiring tests (test_gene_expression_wiring.py) check that gex events fire and respect KO filters but do not pin trajectories. A future commit could add a gex-on fixture for end-to-end equivalence checks.

The gex propensity cache assumes machinery scalars (state.rnap_free, ribosome_free, degradosome_free) and promoter strengths are constant across a run. This holds for every rule in the production rule list today; if a future rule mutates them, set self._gex_props_dirty = True from that rule's apply path or the cache will be stale.

MCC at gex_on is NOT measured here. This fact is wall-time only. A separate measurement (planned step 7) will run the v15 detector with gex_on across the full 455-gene panel and record the new MCC as a separate fact (mcc_against_breuer_v16_gex_compiled or similar). The honest comparison is 'v15 = MCC 0.5372 without gex; v16 = MCC X with gex' as two separate measurements.

Extrapolation to the full 458-gene sweep at scale=0.05 with Rust + 4 workers (the production config used in mcc_v15_replicates): gex_off ~50 min (unchanged from phase 1); gex_on extrapolates to ~65 min via 1.29x scaling. A pre-flight check on a 10-20 knockout sample under Rust would tighten this estimate before committing to a 458-gene sweep.
